sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Pitman along South Broadway (the sheet's own lettering also gives it as North Broadway north of East Holly Avenue), from West and East Holly Avenue at the top to Pitman Avenue and the park in the lower part. The sheet is turned on the page so that the streets run diagonally; its scale is 50 feet to an inch. On the west side of Broadway are the Pitman M. E. Church at the top, a long row of dwellings along East Avenue and Broadway, a block of brick-fronted stores (C.B. construction, coloured blue) and the post office at the corner of 2nd Avenue. East of Broadway the blocks hold stores, an auto sales and service building with garage, and a large movie theatre (Movies) on Theatre Avenue, lettered also as East Driveway. Pitman Title and Trust Co. and the Pitman Natl Bank and Trust Co. stand on the Broadway frontage, with a row of stores facing Pitman Avenue. Further east, past Simpson Avenue, are dwellings, a tile building and The Pitman Grove Review printing works near Montgomery Avenue and Commerce Avenue. The railroad (W. J. & S. R. R., also marked P. R. R.) runs diagonally across the right side with Pitman Passenger Station, a waiting shed, a freight house and a platform beside West Jersey Avenue at the foot of the sheet. The large open block south of Pitman Avenue is marked Park. Water pipes of several sizes are shown dashed in the streets, and a compass rose and the scale bar appear in the lower right. Adjoining sheets are numbered 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 3 around the margins.
notes: West Holly Avenue and East Holly Avenue keep their names in OpenStreetMap; the printed North Broadway and South Broadway are North Broadway and South Broadway.
1st Avenue, 2nd Avenue, 12th Avenue, Northeast Avenue and Southeast Avenue belong to the Pitman Grove radial street system and are footways in OpenStreetMap, so they were not used as control.
Commerce Avenue is lettered on the right edge of the sheet, where it meets East Holly Avenue.
Scale 50 ft. Downtown: South (North) Broadway between West/East Holly and Pitman Avenues, Theatre Avenue, Simpson Avenue, railroad and passenger station, park. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the south-western edge of the built-up part of Pitman, on both sides of the railroad. The sheet is turned on the page (scale 50 feet to an inch) so that the main railroad, lettered W. J. & S. R. R., crosses it from the lower left to the top centre. In the upper left a small group of narrow lots along East Avenue and between East Avenue and a lane faces Laurel Avenue and the South Avenue crossing, with dwellings numbered in the 200 and 100 series. Snyder Avenue runs south-west beside the railroad on the west side, nearly all of it open ground belonging to the adjoining sheet 4. South Broadway and West Jersey Avenue converge at a point where the two streets meet beside the tracks, forming a long triangular block of dwellings with 300-series numbers. On the east side of Broadway are two full residential blocks of frame dwellings and outbuildings between Grandview Avenue and Crafton Avenue, and between Crafton Avenue and Wildwood Avenue, bounded on the east by Oakcrest Avenue. The Pitman Presbyterian Church, lettered Pitman Presbyn Church, stands in the block between Crafton and Wildwood Avenues. A row of small attached outbuildings and a dwelling marked tile appear in the block west of Broadway Avenue north of Crafton Avenue. Water mains of 3, 4, 6 and 8 inches are marked in the streets, many labelled N.J.C.A. The compass rose lies at the lower left, the scale bar at the foot, and neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 5, 10, 12 and 14 are named at the margins.
notes: South Avenue, East Avenue and Snyder Avenue appear with the same names in OpenStreetMap; Snyder Avenue is a short street beside the railroad.
South Broadway and West Jersey Avenue meet in two OpenStreetMap nodes about 42 m apart; the sheet draws one junction at the point of the triangle.
Oakcrest Avenue has two nodes at Wildwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap (a jog about 70 m long); the western node was used as the Oakcrest and Wildwood junction on this sheet.
Scale 50 ft. East/Laurel Avenue corner, South Broadway and West Jersey Avenue at the railroad, Grandview to Wildwood Avenue blocks, Presbyterian church. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows a residential district on the south-western side of Pitman, between Laurel Avenue at the top and South Driveway near the foot. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, so the streets run nearly up and down the sheet. Four parallel streets, West Avenue, Wesley Avenue and The Boulevard, with Chestnut Avenue crossing them at right angles, divide the area into narrow blocks of frame dwellings, each with its outbuildings; house numbers run in the 300 and 400 series. Water mains marked N.J.C.A. run in several streets, and a 94,000 gallon standpipe is shown with a circular tank in the block between West and Wesley Avenues near the top. In the upper right Legion Court runs diagonally from Laurel Avenue to a small circle where it meets two further short streets, and a pair of blue-coloured long buildings marked Iron Parts and Cement Block stand beside the circle. To the east a long diagonal row of dwellings faces Snyder Avenue, which lies along the western side of the railroad (W. J. & S. R. R., P. R. R.). West Jersey Avenue runs on the far side of the tracks, with Young Avenue lettered near the lower right corner. East Avenue and Enbury Avenue are shown ending against Laurel Avenue at the head of the sheet. The sheet adjoins sheets 3, 5, 14, 18 and 19, which are named in the margins. A compass rose and the scale bar are at the lower right and bottom.
notes: The sheet prints Enbury Avenue; OpenStreetMap has Embury Avenue.
The Boulevard is Boulevard Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
South Driveway is Edsam Avenue in OpenStreetMap; it was matched on the sheet by the junctions with West Avenue, Wesley Avenue and The Boulevard.
Scale 50 ft. West Avenue to The Boulevard, Laurel Avenue to South Driveway (OSM Edsam Avenue), Legion Court, Snyder Avenue. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows Pitman Grove, the Methodist camp-meeting ground at the centre of Pitman, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The grove is laid out as a wheel: an oval Circle Avenue around the Auditorium, from which twelve numbered avenues, 1st to 12th Avenue, radiate to an outer square bounded by North Avenue at the top, West Avenue on the west and East Avenue on the east, with Northwest, Northeast, Southwest and Southeast Avenues cutting off the corners. Below South Avenue a rectangular grid of blocks runs down to Laurel Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Wesley Avenue, The Boulevard and Embury Avenue, with Legion Court at the lower right. The radial avenues are narrow, about 10 ft at the circle and 20 to 25 ft further out, and are lined on both sides with closely packed small frame cottages, numbered individually, many of them one- and two-storey dwellings set on narrow lots; the wedge-shaped blocks between them are numbered 22 to 35. Buildings of note are the Auditorium in the centre, an octagonal Pavilion at South Avenue and Wesley Avenue, a Fire Patrol house by the small triangular Summit Park at Southwest Avenue, and an office building on Circle Avenue. Water mains of the N.J.C.A. run along North, South and West Avenues and 7th Avenue. A row of dwellings along the west side of West Avenue, and the ends of Webb, 4th and Asbury Avenues north of North Avenue, belong to the edges of neighbouring sheets 19, 21 and 6. The page is turned so that the grove's square sits upright, which puts north about 36 degrees clockwise of straight up.
notes: The Boulevard is Boulevard Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The radial avenues (1st to 12th) and Circle Avenue are footways in OpenStreetMap and were not used as control.
Auditorium, Pavilion and Fire Patrol house of the Pitman Grove camp meeting.

Southeast Avenue meets East Avenue on the sheet; the OpenStreetMap South Avenue / Southeast Avenue node beside Embury Avenue was excluded, as was South Avenue / West Avenue, which the detector placed 40 ft off.
Scale 50 ft. Pitman Grove camp meeting: radial 1st-12th Avenues around Circle Avenue and the Auditorium, grid south to Laurel Avenue. Page turned about 36 degrees. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers a residential and commercial district in the north-west of Pitman, west of North Broadway and south of McClelland Avenue. McClelland Avenue runs along the top edge, North Broadway along the right edge and North Avenue along the bottom. Oak Avenue crosses the upper right quarter and meets West Holly Avenue, which runs diagonally across the middle of the sheet from the left to the right edge. Along the top is a row of detached frame dwellings with small outbuildings on deep lots. At the right, between Oak Avenue and North Broadway, are the sheet's main non-residential buildings: a large concrete and brick auto repair and storage building for new cars, a showroom, an undertaker, a wagon shed, the 1st Baptist Church with its parsonage, a garage for sixty cars, and the Municipal Building with Fire Department No. 3. A group of long, narrow auto houses, tied to a repair shop, stands in the angle between West (Maple) Avenue and Walnut Avenue at the left. Below West Holly Avenue the blocks are divided into narrow, uniform lots built up with frame dwellings, with a tile dwelling and a concrete block building near Asbury Avenue and a large vacant hall of two storeys on 4th Avenue. Water pipes of 3, 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes marked. Streets are 30 to 50 ft wide. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 36 degrees on the page; the north arrow is at the left. Adjoining sheets are 21 to the west, 22 to the north-east, 7 to the east, 2 to the south-east and 5 to the south.
notes: West (Maple) Avenue: OpenStreetMap has West Avenue at this location.
Oak Avenue is North Oak Avenue and South Oak Avenue today.
Asbury Avenue has no counterpart in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Modern Webb Avenue / West Holly Avenue junction lies 7 m from the drawn one and was rejected by the detector.
Scale 50 ft. McClelland to North Avenue, Oak Avenue to North Broadway; turned about 36 degrees. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers a residential district in the north-east of Pitman, on the east side of North Broadway and west of the railroad. North Broadway forms the left edge of the sheet; Montgomery Avenue runs down the right side beside the multiple tracks of the railroad, which cross the lower right corner and leave the area east of them blank. Evergreen Avenue runs along the top and slopes down towards Montgomery Avenue; Oakland Avenue joins it from the north and continues a short distance south of it, and Myrtle Avenue, Arbutus Avenue, Hazel Avenue and East Holly Avenue follow in turn towards the bottom, each running at an angle to the sheet edges. Blocks 9 to 13 are laid out in long narrow lots, mostly with one dwelling and a small outbuilding apiece, though several lots in blocks 9 and 10 near the top are large and almost empty. The few buildings other than dwellings are a concrete garage for twenty cars on North Broadway at Myrtle Avenue, a plumbing shop, a carpenter shop, and several stores along North Broadway at Arbutus and Hazel Avenues. A strip east of the railroad is labelled Tulip Avenue, not open. Four-inch and eight-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets with hydrants. Streets are 30 to 50 ft wide. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 37 degrees on the page; the north arrow is at the lower right. Adjoining sheets are 22 to the north, 6 to the west and 2 and 8 to the south and east.
notes: Tulip Avenue is marked 'not open' on the sheet.
The railroad beside Montgomery Avenue is lettered W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.); OpenStreetMap names it Vineland Secondary.

The detector found no junction on North Broadway at Myrtle, Arbutus or East Holly Avenues, where the sheet ends before the street centre line; only the Hazel Avenue junction on North Broadway is used.
Scale 50 ft. Evergreen to East Holly Avenue, North Broadway to Montgomery Avenue and the railroad; turned about 37 degrees. One part; Broadway side weakly controlled.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the north-eastern edge of Pitman's business district along the railroad and East Holly Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch. The railroad (W. J. & S. R. R., also marked P. R. R.) crosses the left side from top to bottom, with Montgomery Avenue and Commerce Avenue running parallel to it on its west and east sides. In the middle of the sheet is the lumber and coal yard of Kandle Bros, lettered Coal, Lime, Cements and Builders Supplies, with lumber sheds, lumber piles, a wooden coal trestle, a standpipe, a concrete storage building of the Highway department and a hardware and paints store at East Holly Avenue. South of East Holly Avenue, C. M. Kandle Lumber and Mill Work occupies the block next to Commerce Avenue with a lumber shed, millwork machinery and power building. North and South Summit Avenue form the central north-south street, lined by dwellings with outbuildings, a dairy house and a number of coops. East of them are the S. Summit St. Public School (hollow-square plan, coloured pink) and, across East Holly Avenue, the large brick Pitman High School, lettered fire proof construction, built 1922. The upper half of the sheet is open land and large unsubdivided blocks, with storage buildings and a cattle run near the tracks; Tulip Avenue is marked Not Opened. Esplanade Avenue, Mount Vernon Avenue and Highland Terrace run north-south on the east side, with Glenmere Avenue at the upper right corner. The compass rose is at the centre right and the scale bar at the lower right.
notes: Highland Terrace is lettered with Woodlyn Avenue in parentheses; OpenStreetMap has Woodlynne Avenue north of East Holly Avenue and Highland Terrace to its south.
The sheet prints Mt. Vernon Avenue; today it is Mount Vernon Avenue.
Tulip Avenue is lettered 'Not Opened' west of Esplanade Avenue.
The fitted scale is about 2.6 percent smaller than on neighbouring 50-foot sheets.
Scale 50 ft. Kandle Bros yard, Summit Avenue, Pitman High School, Montgomery and Commerce Avenues by the railroad; fitted 7.8 px/ft (2.6 percent under the atlas scale). One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers a residential district on the north-eastern side of Pitman, divided by East Holly Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page, so East Holly Avenue crosses it from the left, slightly rising to the right, and the cross streets run up and down. North of East Holly Avenue three blocks lie between Highland Terrace (with Woodlyn Avenue lettered in parentheses), Linden Avenue, Fernwood Avenue and Brentwood Avenue, bounded at the top by Glenmere Avenue. The blocks are lined with frame dwellings and outbuildings numbered in the 10 to 60 and 160 to 322 series on the street frontages, with large unbuilt rear portions. Several pairs of dwellings with coloured party strips stand in the block between Highland Terrace and Linden Avenue. The upper-right block between Fernwood and Brentwood Avenues is largely vacant. South of East Holly Avenue are Highland Terrace and Fernwood Avenue running south, with two blocks of dwellings to their sides and a large open tract at the right, numbered with neighbouring sheet 25. Water mains of 4 and 8 inches are shown dashed in the streets. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 8, 11, 23 and 25. The compass rose is at the lower right and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: Highland Terrace is lettered with Woodlyn Avenue in parentheses north of East Holly Avenue; OpenStreetMap has Woodlynne Avenue there and Highland Terrace to the south.
The printed Fernwood Avenue and Brentwood Avenue are North and South Fernwood Avenue and North and South Brentwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Scale 50 ft. North of East Holly Avenue: Highland Terrace (Woodlyn Avenue), Linden, Fernwood, Brentwood Avenues; Glenmere Avenue at the top. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows the southern part of Pitman's business district on either side of Pitman Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page, with the railroad (W. J. & S. R. R., also marked P. R. R.) running diagonally across the upper left. North of Pitman Avenue, between the railroad and Commerce Avenue, stand the A. S. Clark and Son coal, lime, cement and feed warehouse with its concrete bins, and a row of stores facing Pitman Avenue. East of Commerce Avenue is the large Riley Milk, Ice and Cold Storage Co. building (coloured blue, with ice storage, steel frame and pilastered walls), together with a hay and wire warehouse, an auto-washing building, a wagon storage shed and a row of dwellings along Summit Avenue and Mount Vernon Avenue. South of Pitman Avenue West Jersey Avenue runs beside the tracks, with a bowling alley, a large garage with machine shop, a battery charging and upholstering shop, a series of long cinder-block garages, and at the bottom the White Star and Pitman Laundry beside Grandview Avenue. Oakcrest Avenue forms the middle street of the southern half, with dwellings on its east side and a large open block (numbered 54) to Morris Avenue at the right. Water mains of 2, 4 and 6 inches are marked along the streets. Neighbouring sheets named at the margins are 2, 3, 8, 11 and 12. The compass rose is in the lower right and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: Summit Avenue is printed without a North or South prefix; OpenStreetMap has South Summit Avenue on this sheet.
The sheet prints Mt. Vernon Avenue; today it is Mount Vernon Avenue.
At Pitman Avenue the Commerce Avenue junction was measured on the sheet about 3.9 m from the modern OpenStreetMap node; the other junctions fit within 2.3 m.
Summit Avenue north of Pitman Avenue and Oakcrest Avenue south of it are offset by about 22 m, matching the jog in OpenStreetMap.
Scale 50 ft. Pitman Avenue south side, West Jersey, Oakcrest, Grandview, Morris Avenues. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows a block of central Pitman drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Pitman Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east about a third of the way down, with Grandview Avenue along the foot of the sheet. Mount Vernon Avenue bounds the northwest corner, Morris Avenue and Highland Terrace run north and south through the middle, and Fernwood Avenue forms the east side, jogging about 195 feet to the east where it crosses Pitman Avenue. The sheet is turned about 24 degrees from north, so the streets read as horizontal and vertical on the page. Frame dwellings with outbuildings fill most of the lots, set in generous yards; several large lots south of Pitman Avenue carry a single house, and a number of lots are drawn empty. The largest building is Hotel Pitman, a frame hotel of two and three storeys with its own light and electric service, standing on the east side of Highland Terrace north of Pitman Avenue. Beside it are Hotel Pitman Annex and a long row of small iron-clad partition sheds. A plumbing shop, a bake shop with a portable oven, and a few stores and garages are lettered among the dwellings north of Pitman Avenue. Water pipes (4 inch and 6 inch) are marked in the streets, and street widths of 50 feet and 33 feet are noted. Neighbouring sheets are named in the margins: 8 and 9 to the north, 10 to the west, 12 and 13 to the south, and 25 to the east.
notes: Fernwood Avenue is drawn in two offset pieces, north and south of Pitman Avenue; today both pieces are South Fernwood Avenue, joined to Pitman Avenue at two nodes about 55 m apart.
Harding Ct., lettered at the east edge, is Harding Court today.
Sheet is turned about 24 degrees from north (fitted rotation 23.7 degrees, 7.98 px per foot).
Scale 50 ft. Mount Vernon to Fernwood Avenue, Pitman to Grandview Avenue; Fernwood jogs at Pitman Avenue (two OSM nodes). One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a residential district in the south-east of Pitman, east of the railroad and South Broadway. It is bounded by Grandview Avenue at the top, Columbia Avenue at the bottom, Highland Terrace on the east and Oakcrest Avenue on the west; Morris Avenue ends at Grandview Avenue on the top edge. The sheet holds three full blocks, numbered 57, 58 and 160. Oakcrest Avenue does not run straight through: north of Wildwood Avenue it forms the west edge of the sheet, and south of Wildwood it continues about one lot-row further east, so block 160 between Wildwood and Columbia Avenues is set back from the western margin, where the corner of sheet 14 is left blank. The blocks are divided into narrow, deep house lots, most built on with one- and two-storey frame dwellings (yellow) with small frame auto houses at the rear; a few dwellings and outbuildings are of brick or concrete block. The only non-residential buildings are the Christian and Missionary Alliance Church and its rectory, both frame, at the corner of Crafton and Oakcrest Avenues, facing Oakcrest. Four-inch water pipes are drawn along each street, with hydrants at several corners. The streets are drawn 40 to 50 ft wide. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 24 degrees on the page so that the street grid runs square to it; the north arrow sits in the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 10 and 11 to the north, 3 to the west, 13 and 15 to the east, 14 to the south-west and 16 to the south.
notes: Oakcrest Avenue jogs east at Wildwood Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two separate Oakcrest Avenue / Wildwood Avenue junctions about 75 m apart.
Christian and Missionary Alliance Church and rectory at Crafton and Oakcrest Avenues.
Scale 50 ft. Grandview to Columbia Avenue, Oakcrest Avenue to Highland Terrace; Oakcrest jogs east at Wildwood (two OSM nodes). Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers a residential block group in the southeast part of the borough, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. South Woodbury Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and is slightly slanted on the page, Fernwood Avenue crosses the middle, and Highland Terrace runs along the foot. Grandview Avenue, Crafton Avenue and Wildwood Avenue are the three cross streets, running from the top to the bottom of the sheet. The sheet is turned about 66 degrees, with north toward the left of the page, so the streets that run west to east on the ground are the vertical ones here. The blocks are long and mostly undivided; frame dwellings with small outbuildings stand along the street frontages and much of the land behind them is open. The one non-residential building is the Church of Good Shepherd, a church lettered with hot air heat, electric light, pilastered walls and a 32 foot width, on the north side of Highland Terrace between Crafton and Wildwood Avenues. Water mains of 4 inch and 6 inch pipe are shown in the streets, and street widths of 50 feet and 54 feet are noted. The margins give the neighbouring sheets: 25 and 11 to the west, 12 to the south, and 15 to the east. A scale bar of 50 feet to an inch is printed at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Fernwood Avenue is South Fernwood Avenue today; South Woodbury Avenue is South Woodbury Road.
Sheet is turned about 66 degrees from north (north toward the left); fitted rotation -67.0 degrees, 7.96 px per foot.
Scale 50 ft. South Woodbury Avenue to Highland Terrace, Grandview to Wildwood Avenue; turned about -67 degrees (north to the left). One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the southwest side of the central district at 50 feet to an inch. The principal street is South Broadway, which crosses the sheet on a slant from the top towards the bottom; Oakcrest Avenue runs down the east side. Wildwood Avenue, Columbia Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Washington Avenue cross from east to west and meet South Broadway at successive angles, with West Jersey Avenue, Young Avenue, Bellevue Avenue and Villa Avenue joining from the west side. A garage lies on the north side of Columbia Avenue next to South Broadway, a concrete-floored building with a show room and an auto repair shop, lettered heat steam, lights electric, sand buckets and fire extinguishers; beside it are a cinder block store and a second block-built building. Dwellings are frame, in a few cases brick, and stand on narrow lots along Columbia and Lexington Avenues; a metal roofing and sheet metal works occupies a corner on the south side of Lexington Avenue, and an auto truck storage building lies on Oakcrest Avenue. The west and southwest parts are blank, being the part of the sheet outside the mapped area (the margins name sheets 4, 3, 12, 16 and 18). Parallel lines along the far west edge, beside West Jersey Avenue, appear to be the railroad. Water pipes of 4 inch and 6 inch size are marked in the streets.
notes: South Broadway is a slanted street; the sheet has a large blank area at the southwest that belongs to other sheets.
Oakcrest Avenue jogs at Wildwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap (two nodes); the eastern node was used.
Sheet is turned about 24 degrees from north (fitted rotation 23.6 degrees, 8.02 px per foot).
Scale 50 ft. South Broadway, Columbia, Lexington, Washington, Oakcrest Avenues; blank south-west area. One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 lies in the southeastern part of the borough and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It is the next sheet east of sheet 13 and repeats its layout: South Woodbury Avenue runs along the top, slightly slanted on the page, Fernwood Avenue crosses the middle, and Highland Terrace runs along the foot of the sheet. Columbia Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Washington Avenue are the three cross streets, running from top to bottom. The sheet is turned about 66 degrees, so north lies to the left of the page. The blocks are long and mostly open, with frame dwellings facing the streets, small outbuildings behind, and one brick-coloured dwelling in the lower left corner. The upper blocks, numbered 162, 166 and 170, are largely empty land; the lower blocks, 161, 165 and 169, carry more houses, especially along Lexington and Washington Avenues. A dwelling and outbuildings stand beyond the street at the top right, near the edge of the sheet. Water pipes of 4 inch and 6 inch size run in the streets, and street widths of 40 feet, 50 feet and 54 feet are noted. The margins give the adjoining sheets: 13 to the west, 12 and 16 to the south, and 16 to the east.
notes: Fernwood Avenue is South Fernwood Avenue today; South Woodbury Avenue is South Woodbury Road.
Columbia Avenue meets Highland Terrace on the sheet and in OpenStreetMap.
Sheet is turned about 66 degrees from north (north toward the left); fitted rotation -66.5 degrees, 7.97 px per foot.
Scale 50 ft. South Woodbury Avenue to Highland Terrace, Columbia to Washington Avenue; turned about -66 degrees. One part.

sheet-16-1.description: The main part of sheet 16 covers the southern edge of Pitman and the adjoining corner of Glassboro Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. It runs from Columbia Avenue at the top to Madison Avenue and Monroe Avenue at the bottom, and from South Broadway on the west to South Woodbury Avenue on the east, with Oakcrest Avenue and Highland Terrace crossing it north to south and Lexington, Washington, Adams and Jefferson Avenues east to west. Seneca Avenue, Longmere Avenue and Park Avenue meet South Broadway at the left edge. The dash-dot line of the borough limits, lettered Pitman above and Glassboro below, crosses the sheet diagonally from Longmere Avenue towards the north-east, and the blocks south of it are lettered Glassboro Township. The two blocks between Columbia and Washington Avenues west of Highland Terrace are built up with frame dwellings; south of Washington Avenue the land is mostly laid out in narrow, still vacant building lots, with scattered dwellings along Jefferson and Madison Avenues and South Broadway. Buildings of note are the Elwood Kindle Public School, a two-storey fireproof building of 1926 on Washington Avenue east of Highland Terrace, and the H. and R. Dye Stick Works, two small frame buildings nearby. Four-inch water pipes run along most streets, with an eight-inch main on South Broadway. The upper right corner of the page and the lower right triangle hold two insets drawn at the same scale (parts 2 and 3 of the sheet); a heavy line divides them from this part.
notes: South Woodbury Avenue is South Woodbury Road today.
Elwood Kindle Public School, built 1926, on Washington Avenue at Highland Terrace.
H. and R. Dye Stick Works on Washington Avenue east of the school.

Scale 100 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Columbia to Monroe Avenue, South Broadway to South Woodbury Avenue, borough line to Glassboro Township); 2 inset top right (blocks 228/229 on Delsea Drive, C. W. Kensey & Son slaughter house), not placed; 3 inset lower right (Delsea Drive at Pitman Avenue and Cross Keys Road, Atlantic City Electric substation, Cresse's Lake), anchored on one hand-picked junction.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset top right: blocks 228 and 229 on Delsea Drive (Glassboro Road) east of South Woodbury Road, C. W. Kensey & Son slaughter house (no street junction; only Delsea Drive is drawn; needs parcel corners (locate.py corner) or a feature shared with a placed sheet).

sheet-16-3.description: This inset in the lower right of sheet 16 shows a separate area north-east of the main part, on Delsea Drive (lettered also Glassboro Road) where Pitman Avenue meets it from the west and Cross Keys Road, also called Chapel Heights Road, leaves it to the east, with Downer Road branching south-east from Cross Keys Road. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and at the same rotation as the main map. The borough limit between Pitman and Mantua runs along the west side of Delsea Drive, and the land east of it is lettered Mantua Township. The principal building is the Atlantic City Electric Company's Pitman substation, a brick building with a storage and switchboard room and a chemical truck house, on the east side of Delsea Drive beside a stream running into Cresse's Lake, which fills the bottom of the inset. Across Cross Keys Road stand a concrete auto repair shop and a frame store with gasoline tanks, and a few frame dwellings line Cross Keys Road towards Wilson Court at the right edge. West of Delsea Drive, between Pitman Avenue and the heavy dividing line, is a single dwelling with a dog kennel. Most of the frame is blank and marked no exposure.
notes: Cross Keys Road and Downer Road correspond to today's Pitman-Downer Road and Chapel Heights Road; their modern junctions do not match the drawn spacing (about 140 m between Pitman Avenue and Pitman-Downer Road on Delsea Drive today against about 115 m drawn), so the part is placed from Delsea Drive / Pitman Avenue alone.
Atlantic City Electric Company Pitman substation on Delsea Drive.

Scale 100 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Columbia to Monroe Avenue, South Broadway to South Woodbury Avenue, borough line to Glassboro Township); 2 inset top right (blocks 228/229 on Delsea Drive, C. W. Kensey & Son slaughter house), not placed; 3 inset lower right (Delsea Drive at Pitman Avenue and Cross Keys Road, Atlantic City Electric substation, Cresse's Lake), anchored on one hand-picked junction.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset top right: blocks 228 and 229 on Delsea Drive (Glassboro Road) east of South Woodbury Road, C. W. Kensey & Son slaughter house (no street junction; only Delsea Drive is drawn; needs parcel corners (locate.py corner) or a feature shared with a placed sheet).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the southern edge of Pitman and the adjoining part of Glassboro Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 36 degrees on the page so that South Broadway runs straight down the right edge. Longmere (Glen Lake) Avenue runs along the top, where the dash-dot borough line, lettered Pitman above and Glassboro below, divides the two municipalities; Jefferson Avenue and Madison Avenue meet South Broadway at the upper right. Within Glassboro Township, Park Avenue, Central Avenue, Euclid Avenue and Silver Avenue cross the sheet, with the Boulevard, Orienta Terrace and Carpenter running north to south. In the upper left, West Jersey Avenue and Cedar Avenue run beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks, which cross the left side of the sheet diagonally. Most of the ground is laid out in large, sparsely built blocks numbered 174 to 177 and 237 to 242, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings and chicken coops; the lower half is largely vacant. Buildings of note stand on Park Avenue near South Broadway: an iron standpipe 128 ft high holding 78,000 gallons and a pump house kept for reserve of the Borough of Glassboro water works, and a concrete-block garage for twelve cars with a show room. Water pipes of four to eight inches run along Park Avenue and South Broadway. A stream crosses Longmere Avenue near the top edge towards Glen Lake on sheet 18.
notes: Longmere Avenue is lettered Longmere (Glen Lake) Avenue; OpenStreetMap has both Longmere Avenue and Glen Lake Avenue.
Carpenter is Carpenter Street today.
Iron standpipe and pump house of the Borough of Glassboro water works (reserve) on Park Avenue.
Placed from three detected junctions in the lower left and one hand-picked junction (Longmere Avenue / South Broadway) in the top right corner; medium to low confidence.

Scale 100 ft. Glassboro Township south of Longmere (Glen Lake) Avenue: Park, Central, Euclid, Silver Avenues, Orienta Terrace, Carpenter; Glassboro water works standpipe. Turned about 36 degrees. One part, few junctions.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the south-west of Pitman, on the borough's boundary with Glassboro Township. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 37 degrees on the page. Florence Avenue forms the top of the built part, Longmere (Glen Lake) Avenue and the borough limits the bottom, South Broadway the right edge and Cedar Avenue, beside the Mantua Township boundary, the left edge. A railroad (W. J. & S. R. R.) crosses the middle diagonally from lower left to upper right, with West Jersey Avenue and Snyder Avenue running alongside it. North-west of the railroad, the Alcyon area is laid out in blocks 222 to 225 and 151 and 152 between Florence Avenue, Edsam Avenue and Alcyon Boulevard, cut by Long, Lincoln, West and Wesley Avenues. Most of its lots are narrow and empty, with a few frame dwellings; a stream runs across the lower left and Alcyon Boulevard follows it. South-east of the railroad, blocks 68, 153, 172 and 173 along South Broadway, Bellevue (Heck), Villa and Seneca Avenues are more closely built with frame dwellings, with a garage for fifteen cars at Villa Avenue and a tile dwelling near Seneca Avenue. Glen Lake lies in the lower middle, bordered by Glen Lake Avenue. Below the borough limits, on the edge of the sheet, is the Boulevard district of block 174. Water pipes are drawn in the streets with hydrants. The north arrow is at the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 19 to the north, 4 to the north-east, 14 and 16 to the east and 17 to the south.
notes: Alcyon Boulevard here matches the OpenStreetMap junction Alcyon Boulevard / Snyder Avenue / Wesley Avenue at the railroad.
Pine is lettered without a suffix; OpenStreetMap carries this line as part of Alcyon Boulevard.
Cedar Avenue lies on the borough boundary; its junctions carry residuals of 3 to 4 m and Cedar / Edsam was rejected at 11 m.
Fitted with a second-order polynomial; first-order fits leave residuals of 3 to 4 m on Long, West and Wesley Avenues.

Scale 100 ft. South-west Pitman: Florence to Longmere (Glen Lake) Avenue, Cedar Avenue to South Broadway, Glen Lake, railroad, borough limit with Glassboro Township. One part. Cedar Avenue left out of control (junctions 3.8 m, Cedar/Edsam 11 m: displaced).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the western part of central Pitman, between Lakeview and Cleveland Avenues at the top and Florence and Edsam Avenues at the bottom, from the Mantua Township side on the left to the recreation ground on the right. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 37 degrees on the page, with the north arrow at the top. Cedar Avenue, Centre Avenue and Lincoln Avenue run down the sheet and are crossed by Grant, McKinley, Roosevelt Terrace, Laurel, Carew, Tuohy and Florence Avenues, making a regular grid of blocks numbered 140 to 150 and 173 to 185. The middle blocks between Cedar and Lincoln Avenues are the most built up, with rows of frame dwellings on narrow lots, the Masonic Club at Lincoln and McKinley Avenues, and a bowling alley and a store on Cedar Avenue near Laurel Avenue. At the top, block 142 holds the W. C. K. Walls Public School, built in 1926 with cinder block bearing walls and brick facing. East of Lincoln Avenue lies a recreation ground with a baseball field, grand stand and pavilion, and an open air movie house stands at Laurel Avenue. West of Centre Avenue and south of Corrigan Avenue most blocks are large and empty, with only scattered houses; the lower left corner is marked vacant beyond. Four-inch water pipes lie in the streets with hydrants. Adjoining sheets are 20 to the west, 21 to the north, 5 to the east, 4 to the south-east and 18 to the south.
notes: The street at the left edge near block 172 is lettered Daladel (checked at full resolution); no such name is in OpenStreetMap.
Laurel (Martin) Avenue jogs where it crosses Cedar Avenue by about 18 m; in OpenStreetMap the Carew and Laurel nodes on Cedar Avenue are 7 m apart, so the Cedar / Laurel junction was excluded.
Corrigan Avenue and the street lettered Daladel are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
W. C. K. Walls Public School was built in 1926.
Scale 100 ft. Lakeview/Cleveland to Florence/Edsam Avenue, Centre, Cedar, Lincoln Avenues; W. C. K. Walls Public School, recreation ground. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the western edge of Pitman around Alcyon Lake, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 45 degrees on the page so that the lake runs from the lower left to the upper right. The lake fills the middle of the sheet. On its north-west shore lies Alcyon Park, an amusement park lettered open during summer, with a roller coaster and its car house, a merry-go-round, the Funny Chase, a shooting gallery, a restaurant, the Summer Theatre with a bowling alley, a poultry shed, the exhibition halls inside a wood fence, shelters and small stands, reached by a driveway. Beyond it to the west are the Fair Grounds with a dashed race track, a wood fence, produce and other sheds, and a note of a frame grand stand 430 ft away. At the upper right, where West Holly Avenue crosses the lake outlet on a bridge, are George Ogden and Son's lumber and building materials yard, with saw mill, lumber sheds, piles and warehouse, and the Municipal Pumping Station with a reservoir. Cedar Avenue runs south from West Holly Avenue along the east side of the lake, crossed by Lake Avenue, and Lakeview Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet from Alcyon Boulevard at the lake shore, lined with a row of frame dwellings. The large blocks 136 and 203 between the lake and Cedar Avenue are mostly vacant. Much of the sheet is open ground with only a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings.
notes: Alcyon Boulevard at Lakeview Avenue is Lakeside Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Alcyon Park amusement park: roller coaster, merry-go-round, Funny Chase, Summer Theatre, bowling alley, shooting gallery.
George Ogden and Son lumber and building materials yard and the Municipal Pumping Station at the lake outlet on West Holly Avenue.
Placed from three detected junctions and one hand-picked junction (Cedar Avenue / West Holly Avenue); low confidence.
Scale 100 ft. Alcyon Lake, Alcyon Park amusement park, Fair Grounds, Ogden lumber yard; Cedar, Lake, Lakeview Avenues. Turned about 45 degrees. One part, few junctions.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the west and north-west of Pitman along West Holly Avenue and Lake Avenue, which run diagonally across the sheet from upper left to lower right. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 45 degrees on the page, so the streets slope across it; the north arrow is at the upper left. Poplar (Linden) Avenue and Elm Avenue form a street crossing West Holly Avenue at right angles in the middle of the sheet, and West Avenue runs down from the lower right. At the right, McClelland Avenue and Woodland Avenue run east to Oak Avenue, and Walnut Avenue and West (Maple) Avenue meet near the right edge. The densest building is along West Holly Avenue and Lake Avenue, where blocks 17A, 18A, 20A, 20B and 21 hold frame dwellings on narrow deep lots. Non-residential buildings include greenhouses on West Holly Avenue and on Lake Avenue, a cinder block bus storage and repair building and a filling station at the upper left, a garage and repair shop and a printing works near Poplar (Linden) Avenue, a row of small numbered buildings behind West Holly Avenue, and the N. J. C. Assn pumping station with a reservoir at the bottom near West Avenue. A stream and pond enter at the upper left corner. The upper and right-hand areas, blocks 19A, 201 and 15, are almost empty, and the top edge is marked No Exposure. Four- and eight-inch water pipes lie in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 20 to the west, 19 and 5 to the south, 6 to the east and 22 to the north-east.
notes: Poplar (Linden) Avenue and Elm Avenue are one street on the sheet; OpenStreetMap's Elm Avenue lies well west of the drawn street and was not used.
West (Maple) Avenue is West Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Fitted from 7 points only, the McClelland Avenue / Poplar Avenue junction carrying about 4 m, so the placement is of medium confidence.
Scale 100 ft. West Holly and Lake Avenues, Poplar (Linden)/Elm, McClelland and Walnut Avenues; turned about 45 degrees. One part, 7 points; OSM Elm Avenue displaced, left out.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the north of Pitman, from Evergreen Avenue at the bottom to open land at the top, and from North Broadway on the left to Esplanade Avenue and the railroad on the right. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 19 degrees on the page, the north arrow standing near the top. North Broadway forms the left edge, running diagonally; Oakland Avenue runs down the middle and is crossed by Cyrus, Colonial, Kenton, Woodland and Evergreen Avenues, which divide the built-up area into blocks 1 to 4, 6, 7, 103 and 104. Montgomery Avenue bends along the right side beside the multiple tracks of the railroad (W. J. & S. R. R.). The blocks are laid out in narrow lots with frame dwellings, with a few of brick or tile, a Highland Chemical Engine Company fire department building on Oakland Avenue at Kenton Avenue, and coops, storage buildings and sheds in the rear of the lots along Evergreen Avenue. Large parts of the sheet are blank: the whole top third, marked Woods and carrying block numbers 101 and 102, the land beyond the railroad in block 8, where only a few buildings stand at the bottom right, and the area east of Edgemoor Avenue. At the lower left, Oak Avenue, Woodland Avenue and McClelland Avenue meet North Broadway, and a few dwellings and a concrete building stand in block 5. Four- and eight-inch water pipes are drawn. Adjoining sheets are 21 to the west, 6 and 7 to the south and 23 to the east.
notes: Edgemoor Avenue is lettered Edgemoor; OpenStreetMap spells it Edgemore Avenue.
Oak Avenue is North Oak Avenue today, and Woodland Avenue west of North Broadway is West Woodland Avenue.
Kenton Avenue meets Montgomery Avenue once on the sheet; OpenStreetMap has two nodes about 40 m apart, and the eastern one was excluded.
The Evergreen / Oakland junction (rejected, 10 m) and the McClelland / North Oak junction (rejected, 17 m) do not agree with the fitted placement.
Scale 100 ft. Cyrus to Evergreen Avenue, North Broadway to Montgomery Avenue and the railroad; turned about 19 degrees. One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the northern edge of the built-up district and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The blocks lie between Edgemoor Avenue and Glenmere Avenue and are laid out in long narrow lots, mostly empty; the north part is an unbuilt subdivision of numbered blocks 106 to 111 with a blank margin above, bounded at the top by a heavy line. The streets crossing from north to south are Esplanade Avenue, Highland Terrace, Linden Avenue, Fernwood Avenue, Brentwood Avenue, Magnolia Avenue and North Woodbury Avenue, and Waverly Avenue crosses east to west twice: once as a short stub between Esplanade Avenue and Highland Terrace, and again as a full street lower on the sheet. Glenmere Avenue runs along the foot. Muriel, Beechwood and Elwood Avenues are lettered at the right edge, east of North Woodbury Avenue. Only a few dwellings have been built, scattered on blocks 118, 122, 123 and 124 and a handful at the lower left. A strip along the left edge is a long lot with a few houses, bounded by the sheet 22 and sheet 8 edges. At the upper right the borough line is lettered and a road runs diagonally across the corner into Washington Township. Water pipes of 4 inch and 6 inch size are marked along a number of the streets, and a width of 50 feet is noted for most streets.
notes: Edgemoor Avenue is spelled Edgemore Avenue in OpenStreetMap; North Woodbury Avenue is North Woodbury Road.
Fernwood Avenue, Brentwood Avenue and Linden Avenue are North Fernwood Avenue, North Brentwood Avenue and Linden Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Waverly Avenue is drawn twice on the sheet, as a short piece at the left and as a long street across the lower part; OpenStreetMap has one Waverly Avenue running through both.
Sheet is turned about 19 degrees from north (fitted rotation 18.6 degrees, 4.01 px per foot).
Scale 100 ft. North edge: Esplanade to North Woodbury Avenue, Edgemoor to Glenmere Avenue; mostly unbuilt lots; north half without junction control. One part.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the north-eastern corner of Pitman, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. North Woodbury Avenue runs down the left edge, Elwood Avenue and Beechwood Avenue cross the lower half, Clinton Avenue runs south from Beechwood Avenue to East Holly Avenue along the bottom edge, and a short Lakeview Avenue leaves Clinton Avenue to the west. Muriel Avenue runs east from North Woodbury Avenue and bends north-east to continue, lettered not open, across Mantua Creek. The upper half is mostly open, unbuilt ground in the large blocks 119, 132 and 136; Mantua Creek winds down from the top of the sheet to the right edge, with the land beyond it lettered Washington Township. On the creek stands the borough's Sewage Disposal Plant, with a pump house, filter basin and septic tank. Houses are concentrated along North Woodbury Avenue and on the lots between Beechwood and Elwood Avenues and along East Holly Avenue, mostly one- and two-storey frame dwellings with a few of concrete block. The main industrial building is George G. Kindle's concrete products and general contracting works, a cement block manufactory with sheds, in block 133 on Elwood Avenue. Four-inch water pipes run along Elwood Avenue and North Woodbury Avenue, which also carries a six-inch main. The ends of Waverly Avenue and Glenmere Avenue appear across North Woodbury Avenue on the left edge, belonging to sheet 23, and Franklin Avenue is lettered below East Holly Avenue at the bottom.
notes: North Woodbury Avenue is North Woodbury Road today.
Muriel Avenue east of its bend is marked not open; the borough Sewage Disposal Plant stands on Mantua Creek beside it.
George G. Kindle concrete products and general contracting (cement block manufacturing) on Elwood Avenue.
Four detected junctions, three of them on Clinton Avenue, plus a hand-picked Elwood Avenue / North Woodbury Road; medium confidence.
Scale 100 ft. North-east: North Woodbury Avenue, Muriel, Beechwood, Elwood, Clinton Avenues to East Holly Avenue; Mantua Creek, sewage disposal plant. One part.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the area around East Holly Avenue, the main east-west street in this part of the borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. East Holly Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet; north of it are the blocks between Glenmere Avenue and East Holly Avenue, divided by Brentwood, Magnolia and North Woodbury Avenues and, further east, a larger area of open land between Elwood Avenue, Lakeview Avenue and Clinton Avenue. South of East Holly Avenue the street grid is formed by Fernwood Avenue, South Woodbury Avenue, Mansfield Avenue, Pitman Avenue, Ardmore Avenue, Wayne Avenue and Grandview Avenue, and Harding Court runs east to west between Fernwood Avenue and South Woodbury Avenue, lined with a row of small matching dwellings. The sheet is turned about 23 degrees from north, so the streets are close to horizontal and vertical on the page. Most buildings are frame dwellings along East Holly and Pitman Avenues and Harding Court, with a large undivided block (52) behind the houses on the west side; the north side of the sheet and the eastern blocks (205, 207, 208, 213, 214, 217 and 218) are largely unbuilt. A few outbuildings and a dwelling stand near Clinton Avenue. Water pipes are marked in many streets and street widths of 45 and 50 feet are noted. The margins name the neighbouring sheets: 9, 23, 24, 11, 13 and 16.
notes: Fernwood Avenue is North Fernwood Avenue (north of East Holly Avenue) and South Fernwood Avenue today.
Brentwood Avenue is North Brentwood Avenue and South Brentwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap; North Woodbury and South Woodbury Avenues are North and South Woodbury Road.
Ardmore is printed without a suffix; OpenStreetMap has Ardmore Avenue.
Sheet is turned about 23 degrees from north (fitted rotation 23.2 degrees, 4.01 px per foot).
Scale 100 ft. East Holly Avenue area: Glenmere to Grandview Avenue, Brentwood to Clinton Avenue, Harding Court. One part.
